title: Spiral barrage
subtitle: Build a readable spiral barrage with a reachable response and a useful recovery.
summary: A rotating emitter releases a stream that traces a spiral.
overview: A rotating emitter releases a stream that traces a spiral, turning projectile timing into a moving lane the player can follow or cross.
learning: Tune the signal, commitment, geometry, response, and recovery of a spiral barrage as one rule.

demo.title: Test the spiral barrage
phaseDescriptions: Show rotation direction, emission rhythm, and the first arm of the spiral before the pattern fills the arena.
The player can move with the rotation, cross one arm during a wide interval, or reposition toward a region where lane spacing is larger.
The emitter stops while the mature spiral arms continue leaving the arena, preventing a new pattern from overlapping an unreadable residue.

steps.title: Can the player read the complete rule?
steps.body: Show rotation direction, emission rhythm, and the first arm of the spiral before the pattern fills the arena.

steps.title: Is the intended response reachable?
steps.body: The player can move with the rotation, cross one arm during a wide interval, or reposition toward a region where lane spacing is larger.

steps.title: Does recovery create a useful outcome?
steps.body: The emitter stops while the mature spiral arms continue leaving the arena, preventing a new pattern from overlapping an unreadable residue.

mistakes.title: Tuning only the first second misses delayed overlaps that make the mature spiral impossible to navigate
mistakes.body: Tuning only the first second misses delayed overlaps that make the mature spiral impossible to navigate.

mistakes.title: The cue and active geometry disagree
mistakes.body: If the visible spiral barrage cue promises a different area or timing, the player cannot carry the learned rule into the next cycle.

designNotes.title: Tune the complete rule
designNotes.body: Coordinate angular velocity, fire interval, projectile speed, and duration; small changes can close every lane several seconds later.

designNotes.title: Escalate one variable at a time
designNotes.body: Reverse rotation, add a second offset arm, or pulse the fire rate after the player has learned the base lane motion.

designNotes.title: Prove the recovery
designNotes.body: The emitter stops while the mature spiral arms continue leaving the arena, preventing a new pattern from overlapping an unreadable residue.

story.title: What the mechanic communicates
story.body: A rotating emitter releases a stream that traces a spiral, turning projectile timing into a moving lane the player can follow or cross. The encounter uses that rule as a short promise: a visible signal, a committed action, and a result the player can verify.

adaptation.title: Adapt it to the player verbs
adaptation.body: The player can move with the rotation, cross one arm during a wide interval, or reposition toward a region where lane spacing is larger. Coordinate angular velocity, fire interval, projectile speed, and duration; small changes can close every lane several seconds later.

distinction.title: Keep the mechanic distinct
distinction.body: Tuning only the first second misses delayed overlaps that make the mature spiral impossible to navigate. Do not hide that distinction behind extra effects or tracking that the announced rule does not contain.

lensNotes.body: The signal must reveal the relevant timing and geometry before commitment.
The complete player extent and the active region determine whether the route is real.
The response uses an ordinary supported verb and produces an observable result.
Escalation asks the player to apply the same learned rule under tighter constraints.
